title: codemother proves her dashboard wears the one status label and the inbox's idea and intention counts
intention: The codemother dashboard's half of 'a ticket has ONE status' (ticket 3feb201c84ea) and of 3ed960cc402e clause (5) (the inbox and the dashboard print the same open-idea and open-intention counts) is measured today only from operator_inbox's proofs, which import codemother's dashboard (test_one_status_everywhere.py:80, test_operator_inbox.py:295), a RULE 1 breach. Codemother's own proof holds it here.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: encapsulation_holds names cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_one_status_everywhere.py:80, cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py:295 and cairn/tools/operator_inbox/probes/one_status_everywhere.py:57. RULE 1: a ticket's proofs measure only that component, so the dashboard's teeth berth with codemother before operator_inbox drops its copies.
traces_to: CLAUDE.md RULE 1; outline 2.3.7.1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any tool it publishes); outline 17.13.1.
how: New proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_the_dashboard_wears_the_one_label.py builds the seven-ticket fixture (THINKME, TICKETME:waiting, PROVEME:waiting, WATCHME(fx):waiting, WATCHME(fx), PROVED, a prose cursor), renders format_dashboard(data, tickets_dir=) over the inbox's data dict, and compares its printed rows and group headers with operator_inbox.read_tickets and format_summary; a live tooth compares format_dashboard() with the live reader; a count tooth reads the IDEAS and INTENTIONS lines against gather_all()'s counts. No code change.

clauses.claim: every dashboard row over the fixture wears read_tickets' label and the dashboard lists exactly the reader's open set
the dashboard's status groups are the inbox header's counts in the inbox header's order
over the live world format_dashboard() wears read_tickets' label on every open ticket
the dashboard's IDEAS and INTENTIONS counts are gather_all()'s

decisions.text: D1: the dashboard's teeth berth with codemother; operator_inbox drops its copies in its own ticket.
